title: Clarifying the confusion between poligeenan, degraded carrageenan, and carrageenan: A review of the chemistry, nomenclature, and in vivo toxicology by the oral route
authors: McKim JM, Willoughby JA, Blakemore WR, Weiner ML
journal: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
funder: Financial support for the preparation of this review was provided by FMC Corporation. The authors acknowledged the Manager of Global Regulatory Affairs of the FMC Health and Nutrition business unit for comments and support.
authorConflicts: The authors were employees of IONTOX LLC, Celtic Colloids Inc and TOXpertise LLC at the time of publication.
result: Narrative review. Food-grade carrageenan has a weight-average molecular weight of 200,000 to 800,000 Da; poligeenan of 10,000 to 20,000 Da, produced at pH 0.9 to 1.3 above 80 °C for several hours. The review states that gastric pH of 2 to 3, rising towards 5 with food, and gastric emptying of 3 to 4 hours provide insufficient time, temperature and acid for hydrolysis, that carrageenan has never been shown to be converted to poligeenan in vivo, and that carrageenan is not absorbed and does not cause gastrointestinal lesions.
